cards.text: This psalm is of Asaph, and it's written for the choirmaster. It's a song for God's people to sing together. So listen close to how Asaph kicks it off, friend.

cards.question: Asaph opens the psalm by calling for silence before God.

cards.text: And he wants the WHOLE band: a song, the tambourine, the harp and the lyre. I sing to my ovens every morning, and not ONE of them has ever asked for an encore.

cards.question: Next Asaph calls for the ram's horn, and he ties it to the calendar. When should it sound?

answers.text: At the New Moon and the full moon
On the first day of the harvest

cards.question: Asaph gives a reason for all this noise on the feast day. What is it?

answers.text: God made it a statute for Israel

cards.text: Asaph says God set it up as a testimony for Joseph, one of the sons of Jacob. So this isn't just a party, friend, it's a party with a MEMORY, and that memory goes back to a land Israel knew all too well.

cards.question: This testimony for Joseph goes back to the land of ___.

cards.text: Then the psalm says, "…I heard an unfamiliar language…" Now the voice changes, and it's God speaking, looking back at His people carrying heavy loads.

cards.question: God remembers the burden on His people's shoulder. What does He say He did about it?

cards.text: You know the one-trip-from-the-car move, every bag on both arms, fingers turning PURPLE? Now picture all of it lifted off, because God says their hands were freed from the basket.
God goes on: His people called out to Him in distress. You know that voice, friend, the one I use when the timer's going off and my mustache can't find the oven mitt.

cards.question: When His people called out in distress, God says He ___ them.
God says He answered His people from a cloud of thunder.

cards.text: Then God names a place: the waters of Meribah, where the people once quarreled over water (Exodus 17:1-7). I once watched the dead batteries I shared a drawer with argue for a WEEK over who had the most charge left, so I get it.

cards.question: What does God say happened at the waters of Meribah?

cards.text: Then God says, "Hear, O My people, and I will warn you…" When ANYBODY opens like that, friend, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: God says He wishes His people would listen to Him.
God warns Israel about one thing that must never be among them. What is it?

cards.text: Then God reminds them who's talking: the LORD their God, who brought them up out of Egypt. And He says, "Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it."

cards.question: After God offers to fill His people's mouths, He says they listened to Him and obeyed.
Israel won't listen to God. So what does God do?

answers.text: Gives them up to their stubborn hearts

cards.text: Oof, that one stings. But God isn't done, and here comes that wish again: if only His people would listen, if Israel would follow His ways.

cards.question: If Israel would follow His ways, what does God say He'd soon do?

cards.text: Then God talks about those who hate the LORD. And what He says about how they'd act sent both of my bushy eyebrows straight UP.

cards.question: God says those who hate the LORD would truly obey Him.

cards.text: Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, like the coworker who looks SO busy the second the boss walks by. And God says their doom would last forever.
How does God close out this psalm, friend? Not with enemies but with feeding His people, and you KNOW that's my favorite part.

cards.question: If only His people would listen, God says He'd feed them wheat. What kind of wheat?

cards.text: And with honey from the rock, God says He would satisfy them. Honey from a ROCK, friend, and I've stared at plenty of rocks without a single one ever handing me a thing.
